The file has two candidates: `countPrimes` (via `isPrime`) and `dedupe`. I'll time each one separately without modifying the file.
`countPrimes` is the slow part. In my timing run it took about 268 ms, versus about 31 ms for `dedupe`.

It's the `isPrime` trial division inside `countPrimes`. For each `n` up to 60,000 it loops up to `n` when `n` is prime, so the total work is roughly the sum of primes below 60,000, around 1.6×10⁸ modulo operations. `dedupe` is quadratic in principle, but it only does about 10⁸ cheap `includes` comparisons on a small array, so it runs much faster in practice.
